clue.text: Two bulls shared equally?

indicators.note: Two asks for the word given by the following leaf to be written out a second time

parts.note: in darts the bull, or bullseye, scores fifty points

explanation.surface: A question about splitting a pair of bulls evenly between owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' doubles the score for one bull: in darts the inner bullseye is worth fifty, so two bulls read as the score said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a deal split into equal halves between two parties is described this way.

clue.text: Defect in platform, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for platform is to be heard said aloud, not written

parts.note: a floor is a level surface or platform to stand on

explanation.surface: A fault in a stage or railway platform, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech FLOOR and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a defect is a fault or imperfection in something.

clue.text: Structure of class at independent applied to

parts.note: a form is a school class in Britain
on means applied to, as paint is on a wall

explanation.surface: Describes how a class at an independent school is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a school year group or class is a 'form'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an arrangement or shape into which things are set is a structure.

clue.text: Give way to bear

definitions.meaning: to give way is to surrender or submit to pressure
a tree may bear fruit, that is produce a crop

explanation.surface: An instruction to submit to a bear, as if menaced by the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one verb: surrendering to pressure, and producing a harvest or return.

clue.text: Concerned and upset at home, sweat pouring

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: pouring suggests the letters of sweat flowing out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone anxious indoors, sweat streaming down their face.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being worried and agitated is described as being in this state of turmoil.

clue.text: Sporting call from friend in hot pants

indicators.note: in places the word for friend inside the rearranged letters
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of hot are a mess and get rearranged

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend in hot pants shouts something at a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, here an anagram signal, so the hot pants are a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the huntsman's cry on sighting a fox in British fox hunting, a field sport.

clue.text: Touch head of freshwater fish

indicators.note: head of takes just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A command to touch the head of a fish from fresh water.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to touch something is to explore it with the fingers.

clue.text: Medieval hero unfortunately lied about first of conquests

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the selected letter
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of lied are jumbled
first of takes the opening letter of conquests

explanation.surface: A warrior who sadly lied about his first conquests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges LIED into ELID, and 'about' wraps it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Castilian knight Rodrigo Díaz, celebrated hero of Spain's eleventh-century wars.

clue.text: Speculate to accumulate with such a do seller's organised

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of seller's, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A sales event organised by a trader who believes in spending money to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a product sold at a loss to draw customers who then buy more, a gamble on future profit.

clue.text: Song and dance after foremost of people show willing

indicators.note: after places the song and dance behind the chosen letter
foremost of picks the opening letter of people

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: People performing a song and dance to show eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to co-operate or go along with others is to show willing.

clue.text: A European king must go to give assent

indicators.note: must go says the king abbreviation is taken away from the nationality

parts.note: a Greek is a European
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A European monarch must abdicate to grant consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to consent or concur is to give assent.

clue.text: Completely boycotts international team

parts.note: all means completely, as in 'all wrong'
to black something is to boycott it, as unions black goods

explanation.surface: A country is shunned in sport entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'black' goods or firms is an old trade-union term for refusing to deal with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the nickname of New Zealand's national rugby union side.

clue.text: Criminal activity by pop group, I hear

parts.note: a band is a pop group
a judge tries a case, that is hears it in court

explanation.surface: A pop group committing crimes, so the speaker has been told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like gossip; 'hear' is the court sense, to try a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: robbery and lawlessness by outlaws is criminal activity.

clue.text: Sing version with new opening

indicators.note: with new opening says the first letter of the word for version is replaced

parts.note: a model is a version, as a car model

explanation.surface: An instruction to sing a fresh version of a song with a new intro.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter is the new opening; the Y comes from the crossing at 3 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the warbling Alpine style of singing that flips between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Who might observe rarest moon excitedly?

definitions.text: Who might observe rarest moon excitedly?

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitation, so the letters of rarest moon are stirred up

explanation.surface: Asks who would get excited watching an unusual moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a scientist who studies the heavens would watch an unusual moon eagerly.

clue.text: Argue after small child leads one to squalid part of city

indicators.note: after puts the word for argue behind small child

parts.note: a kid is a child
to row is to argue

explanation.surface: A quarrelling little child leads someone to a slum.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a run-down urban district of down-and-outs and cheap lodgings.

clue.text: Go over tries again, against English

indicators.note: against means next to, so the abbreviation sits beside the retrial word

parts.note: a court that rehears a case tries it again

explanation.surface: A court case retried in spite of English opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' looks like opposition but means beside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to practise or run through something again is to go over it.

clue.text: Instrument installed in radio car in avenue

indicators.note: installed in says the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A musical instrument fitted into a radio car parked in an avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Sixth sense in teaching

parts.note: tuition means teaching

explanation.surface: The sixth sense as something learnt in class.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: instinctive knowing without reasoning is called a sixth sense.

clue.text: Farm owner fled, heading for Cheyenne with that woman

parts.note: ran means fled

indicators.note: heading for takes the opening letter of Cheyenne

parts.note: her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A cattle baron flees to Cheyenne with a woman, a Western plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who owns or runs a large livestock farm in the Americas.

clue.text: Offering more space? More, or I misinterpreted

indicators.note: misinterpreted means read wrongly, so the letters of more or I are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they misheard an offer of more space.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a place with greater capacity is more spacious.

clue.text: Board allowed to block head

indicators.note: to block means to sit in the way, so the word for allowed goes inside

parts.note: pate is an old word for head
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A board permitted to block a head, perhaps in a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee; it is the artist's mixing board.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the thin board on which a painter mixes colours.

clue.text: Mine's leading, then this at Grand Prix?

parts.note: a pit is a mine, and the 's stands for is
top means leading

explanation.surface: A driver leading the race then makes this halt at the Grand Prix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine's leading' reads as a boast about one's car; it is PIT'S plus TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the halt for fuel and tyres a racing car makes in the pits during a race.

clue.text: New elected judge, a martial art expert

parts.note: a politician voted in is elected

explanation.surface: A newly elected judge turns out to be a fighting expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Japanese warrior skilled in stealth and ninjutsu.

clue.text: Exposed, corrupt Dane importing kilo …

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the abbreviation goes inside
corrupt means spoilt, so the letters of Dane are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked Dane smuggling a kilo is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges DANE into NAED, and 'importing' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unclothed or uncovered, laid bare.

clue.text: Away team's kit is better

parts.note: out means away, as in 'out of the office'
a strip is a sports team's kit

explanation.surface: A football club's away kit is superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to outrun or surpass someone is to better them.

clue.text: … poor and good quality

parts.note: thin means poor, as a thin excuse

explanation.surface: Continues 23: the corrupt Dane's kilo is poor, yet of good quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a characteristic or attribute, as in 'patience is a fine thing'.

clue.text: Girl from Harlem, Manhattan

indicators.note: from says the name is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A young woman who lives in Harlem in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's given name.

clue.text: Temporary movement following fashion

indicators.note: following places the word for movement after the word for fashion

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it
a shift is a movement or change of position

explanation.surface: A short-lived trend chasing the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to make.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something improvised to serve for now is stopgap.

clue.text: Turn of phrase fool shortened on mobile

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the abbreviation follows
shortened means cut short, so the last letter of the word for fool goes

parts.note: an idiot is a fool
M is the abbreviation for mobile

explanation.surface: A fool trimmed his words when speaking on a mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an expression whose meaning isn't literal, a set phrase.

clue.text: Last in queue after free travel

indicators.note: after puts the final letter behind the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: Last in takes the final letter of queue

explanation.surface: The last person in the queue gets to travel for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like no charge; it is the verb rid.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to journey on a horse, bike or vehicle.

clue.text: Publicity must have appropriate look, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals the phrase is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: proper means appropriate and a gander is a look, as in 'take a gander'

explanation.surface: Advertising needs the right look, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' is informal British for a look; in British speech 'proper gander' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: biased information spread to promote a cause, a form of publicity.
